rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results <U+2013> authors ran HidroMORE (Sentinel-2 NDVI, FAO56 water balance) over the M<U+00E9>denine governorate 2016-2019 and collected gravimetric soil moisture at four orchards. Q2: Validation results, Table 2 and Simulation results, Figs 5-8 <U+2013> model soil water content compared with in-situ measurements (overall R2 0.72, IA 0.76); simulated depletion and stress coefficient mapped by zone, lowest depletion in mountain/piedmont zones with Jessour/Tabia and highest near Dar Dhaoui on poorly evolved soils; Conclusions state the study offers an objective tool to prioritise orchards for intervention. Q4: Table 2, Fig 7A-C <U+2013> soil water content measured and modelled, depletion, Ks and adjusted ET simulated as the intermediate variables between RS inputs and mapped drought stress. Q5: Table 2, Fig 8 <U+2013> results reported separately for four agro-ecological zones (mountain Zammour, piedmont Ksar Djedid, inner plain Dar Dhaoui, coast Zarzis) with different soils and climates. Q6: Model simulation section, Figs 5-8 <U+2013> simulation covers the entire olive area of the governorate (8588 km2, ~200,000 ha olives), results given as regional olive-area percentages. Q7: Discussion (Model evaluation) and Conclusions <U+2013> authors state a finer, accurate soil map with better soil characteristics is crucial for simulation results in coastal/inner plains, and that a denser weather-station network is needed to avoid precipitation misrepresentation. Q8: Discussion <U+2013> persistent overestimation of soil water content, low correlation in Zarzis and Dar Dhaoui, underestimated root-system variability within zones, coarse 1/200,000 soil map, missing 2018 soil moisture data, ET underestimation intrinsic to FAO56 method.
rows.notes: Doubt on Q2: the study produces and validates a drought-stress map and the authors assert it can serve to prioritise interventions, but no prioritisation or intervention outcome is tested; the effectiveness of water harvesting and soil type are simulation findings (parameterised soil types behind Jessour/Tabia), not independently measured. Q3 no: spatial stress distribution comes only from the model; the gravimetric soil moisture serves as validation at four points, not as a second method establishing the prioritisation result. Q9 no: Table 2 gives SD, min, max and RMSE for the soil water content comparison, not dispersion or uncertainty for the mapped stress/prioritisation result; RMSE does not count.

notes: Full text available; figures referenced but not reproduced (no numeric uncertainty on stress maps visible). Single claim row.
